title: Tile Roofing in Sugar Land
description: Sugar Land tile often looks fine from the curb. The underlayment under it is what fails, and walking the field to check breaks more tile.
html:
People searching tile roofing in Sugar Land are usually looking at a concrete or clay roof that still looks sharp, with a leak the ceiling does not line up with. The tile is often fine. The sheet under it is not.

Do not walk it to find out

Tiles crack under a casual boot. The leak path is the underlayment: heat-shrunk felt, nails, hips, and valleys. Rain gets under a sound-looking tile and runs until it finds a seam in the deck. The longer version, for Katy and Cypress as well as Sugar Land, is tile roofs in Houston suburbs. The service page is tile roofs. We do not send a crew across the field just to look.

When the tile should not go back

A few broken tiles and a sound underlayment is a repair, including matching what we can salvage. Underlayment that has turned to paper is a replacement, because lifting the field is already most of the work. Some Sugar Land houses should stay tile. Some are better on stone-coated steel, which keeps a tile profile and takes the concrete weight off the rafters. The photo on this post is that profile, not a clay tile. Say which one the house can carry before anyone orders a pallet.

The city page is residential roofing in Sugar Land. Request a free inspection, or call (281) 541-0027.
